To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Eosin Y is a suitable tool for the detection and visualization of CHC distribution in insects; (2) the surface barrier of Drosophila adults, and of Tenebrio larvae, but not of Locusta nymphs, is regionalized;
the surface of the fly body is not uniform but rather organized into distinct regions that are permeable to Eosin Y at different temperatures.
Eosin Y, a dye commonly used for staining of biological tissues, is an excellent tool for mapping the distribution of surface lipids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regionalization of CHCs in the insect cuticle and the factors that control their distribution.
the regionalization of the cuticular barrier in insects.
the molecular basis of the surface barrier in insects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regionalization of the surface lipids of Drosophila adults is a consequence of the regionalization of gene expression and/or the regionalization of biochemical processes.
Eosin Y is a useful tool to visualize the distribution of surface lipids on insect cuticles.
the cuticular barrier is a complex structure that is regionally organized and that the permeability to water is determined by the composition of CHCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insect body is a mosaic of permeable and impermeable regions that may be used as a model system to study CHC regionalization.
regionalization of CHCs is an important feature of the surface barrier and may be used as a marker for studying CHC production.
the Eosin Y dye is an excellent tool to visualize the surface lipid barrier in insects and other arthropods and to study its dynamics in different life stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface of an insect is not a uniform, homogeneous structure, but a mosaic of regions with different properties.
regionalization of the insect body is not limited to organs and tissues but also applies to surface lipids.
the insect cuticle can be visualized by Eosin Y, which may be used as a simple and inexpensive tool in comparative and ecological studies.
